text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

Australian brewer JAMES MATTHEW TOOHEY was born on this day in 1850. It seems that in the early days in Sydney, your beer preference could be dictated by your religion, as TOOHEY's main rival was the Protestant TOOTH's.
German engineer and pioneer of the modern car engine, RUDOLF DIESEL, was born in 1858.
British Prime Minister from 1937-1940, NEVILLE CHAMBERLAIN, was born in 1869.

Australian cricketer CLEM HILL, known as a talented batsman but better known for his celebrated 1911 punch-up at a selectors' meeting, was born in 1877. CLEM demanded that selectors approved a player-elected manager, and although he won the fight (leaving an Official with a black eye), he lost the battle.
New Zealand/Australian entertainer GEORGE "PAT" HANNA, whose successful career took him to the United States where he was known as "DOWN-UNDER WILL ROGERS", was born in 1888.
English writer WILLIAM HATFIELD, who jumped ship in Australia and worked in the outback while writing "Australia through the windscreen" and "I find Australia", was born in 1892.
American actor PETER GRAVES was born on this day in 1926.

US country singer CHARLEY PRIDE was born in 1938. He was the first black country and western artist to became a superstar. He has had more than 30 number one hits. His biggest was "Kiss An Angel Good Morning" (1971).
Australian jurist MICHAEL KIRBY was born in 1939.
Electronics whiz DICK SMITH, who built his first crystal radio set at the age of seven and sold his electronics empire to become a publisher in 1984, was born in 1944.
US drummer with the 'Doobie Brothers' JOHN HARTMAN was born in 1950.

US singer and actress IRENE CARA was born in 1959. A child star of radio and television, she got her big break with a part in the movie "Fame" in 1980. She was allowed to sing the title song. Other hits included "Flashdance..What A Feeling" (1983) and "Breakdance" (1984).
Us singer/songwriter and PRINCE discovery TAJA SEVELLE was born in 1962. "Love Is Contagious" (1988) was the first hit.
** EVENTS **
1662 : The first public buses, 8-seater vehicles known as
"carrosses a cinq solz", ran in Paris.
1718 : LADY MARY WORTLEY MONTAGU innoculated her son
against the smallpox virus, after learning of the practice while travelling in Turkey. This was the first time innoculation against the disease had been practiced in England.
1834 : In Dorset, England, six labourers were sentenced
to seven years banishment to a penal colony in Australia for forming a trade union. They bacame known as the Tolpuddle Martyrs.
1850 : The AMERICAN EXPRESS Company was formed in
Buffalo, New York.
1871 : The insurrection of Paris against the French
government began. The rebels, known as the Communards, were finally defeated in May.
1891 : The first London to Paris telephone link was
established.
1922 : MAHATMA GANDHI was jailed for civil disobedience.
At the time, he was quoted as saying "It is better to be violent if there is violence in our hearts, than to put on the cloak of non-violence to cover impotence".
1923 : The price of butter in Berlin became so inflated,
that the government decreed that it no longer be served in restaurants. Germans who dined out began taking their own butter with them.
1931 : The American company SCHICK INCORPORATED began
making electric razors.
1944 : Alarm clocks went on sale in Chicago for the first
since the beginning of World War Two. About 2,500 people trampled security-guards and store workers, in their rush to buy a clock.
1949 : The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) was
formed. The Organisation was established to provide collective defence of major Western European and North American States against the perceived threat from the Soviet Union.
1950 : British athlete ROGER BANNISTER ran the first
4-minute mile.
1965 : Soviet cosmonaut ALEKSEI LEONOV became the first
man to walk in space. Secured by a lifeline, he somersaulted and danced in orbit hundreds of kilometres above the Earth, while also taking the first hand-held film images of our planet from space.
1967 : The oil tanker Torrey Canyon was wrecked off the
Cornish coast of England, spilling 919,000 barrels of oil into the sea.
1971 : The first women to win a top level diplomatic post
Dame ANNABELLA RANKIN was named High Commissioner to New Zealand.
1975 : Australian broadcast celebrity GRAHAM KENNEDY was
banned indefinitely from live radio and television for making a crow call, similar to a four-letter word, on his television show. He returned to live radio in June 1975.
1984 : Leading historian GEOFFREY BLAINEY warned that the

rate of Asian migration could threaten Australia's tolerance of immigrants. He said South-East Asians were a favoured majority in Australia's immigration policy. Professor BLAINEY said Asian migration was well ahead of public opinion and that a disproportionate intake could break down the harmony established
over the last 30 years.
1990 : Christian Democrats won a landslide victory in the
first democratic elections held in East Germany.
1993 : After six days of deadlock, security forces
stormed a hijacked Ethiopian airliner in the eastern town of Dire Dawa, killing two of the four hijackers.
